newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel quarterly net tops expectations.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel quarterly net tops expectations.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp. said Wednesday its net income surged in the second quarter, surpassing Wall Street expectations, and the company's stock rose by nearly 9 percent.

Excluding a $1.01-per-share gain on the sale of its equity interest in Iron Ore Co. of Canada, the nation's second biggest steel company arned $47 million, or 32 cents a share, in the latest quarter, compared with $27 million, or 14 cents a share, in the second quarter of 1996.
Bethlehem reported sales of $1.21 billion in the second quarter, compared with $1.24 billion a year ago.
The results easily beat analysts' average forecast of 23 cents a share, according to figures compiled by First Call.
Bethlehem stock rose 81 cents to $10.69 in consolidated late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Results for the quarter improved from a year ago, principally due to improved costs as a result of our restructuring plans and higher realised prices," the company said.

"We are successfully executing our business plans, implementing our restructuring plans, eliminating the significant losses of the restructured businesses and rebuilding our financial strength," Chairman Curtis Barnette said in a statement.

The company said its basic steel operations posted an operating income of $77 million excluding the effects of the gain from the sale of Iron Ore Co., compared with $53 million a year ago. The Iron Ore Co. sale resulted in cash proceeds of $145 million.
Looking ahead, the company said U.S. industry steel shipments in 1997 should be 100 million tons, about equal to the 1996 total.
"The demand from the major steel-consuming sectors continues to be relatively good," the company said.
The company's steel-related operations segment reported losses from operations of $10 million for the second quarter, compared with losses of $8 million a year earlier.
